content.text: When Stripe or PayPal bans your account, it’s not just an inconvenience—it’s a structural rejection. These platforms exclude entire countries based on geopolitical risk, not your business model. Nigeria, alongside Ghana, Kenya, and others, faces this daily. The problem isn’t your product; it’s the [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-automated-digital-product-delivery-crypto-7|The Real]]-behind-how-creators-ghana-get-paid-3|architecture]] you’re forced to rent. Sovereign commerce infrastructure solves this by shifting control to you. No platforms. No subscriptions. No geographic gatekeepers. This analysis compares your real options when conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/get-payment-gateways-cameroon-digital-products-working-today|COREMERCH guide to payment]] processors fail. We’ll break down what each offers, how they handle restricted regions, their costs, and who owns the final system. The goal is clear: replace rented dependency with owned infrastructure.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Platform stripe

Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle are centralized platforms. They offer payment processing, product hosting, and delivery—but only if your country is approved. For Nigeria, these services are unavailable or severely restricted. Workarounds like VPNs or proxy accounts are temporary and risky. Sovereign commerce infrastructure, such as COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack, operates differently. It uses GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. Payments are processed via NOWPayments, supporting 300+ cryptocurrencies with a 0.5% fee. This stack is deployed under your control, not rented from a platform. The tradeoff is clarity: you own the system but must deploy it. No platform lock-in, no geographic restrictions—just infrastructure you control.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Stripe and PayPal exclude countries based on regulatory risk, currency instability, or sanctions. For Nigeria, this means no access. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle follow similar restrictions, often without explanation. Workarounds like using a U.S. bank account or proxy service are fragile and violate terms of service. Sovereign infrastructure bypasses this by operating at the base layer. GitHub Pages, Cloudflare, and Supabase are globally accessible tools. NOWPayments processes crypto payments without KYC or geographic blocks. The Edge Commerce Stack deploys this architecture in 48 hours, configured for your products. It’s not a workaround—it’s a structural alternative. The tradeoff is upfront deployment effort, but the result is permanent access without platform dependency.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Stripe and PayPal charge 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction, but only if you’re allowed to use them. Crypto payments via NOWPayments cost 0.5% with no monthly fees. Recommended networks like BSC, Solana, and TRON keep transaction fees under $0.10. The Edge Commerce Stack costs $197 for deployment, including 5 products loaded, SPF/DKIM/DMARC configuration, and 30-day support. Compare this to Gumroad’s 10% fee or Paddle’s 5% fee, both of which are unavailable in Nigeria. The real cost of sovereign infrastructure is upfront, but ownership eliminates recurring fees. The tradeoff is clear: pay once to own your system, or rent access until the platform rejects you.
Sovereign infrastructure eliminates platform dependency—no more account bans.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With Stripe or PayPal, you rent access to their systems. They control your data, payment flow, and product delivery. If they ban your account, you lose everything. Sovereign infrastructure inverts this. The Edge Commerce Stack deploys on your GitHub or Cloudflare account. Order data is stored in your Supabase database. File delivery uses your Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive. NOWPayments sends automatic webhooks when payments confirm on-chain, triggering instant product delivery. You own the code, the data, and the process. The tradeoff is responsibility: you must manage your system. But the reward is infrastructure sovereignty—no platform can shut you down.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you’re in Nigeria and need immediate sales, sovereign infrastructure is your only permanent solution. Workarounds for Stripe or PayPal are temporary and risky. The Edge Commerce Stack is built for this scenario: deployed in 48 hours, configured for your products, and tested end-to-end. If you’re selling digital products like ebooks, courses, or templates, this architecture automates payment verification and delivery without platform dependency. The tradeoff is upfront cost and deployment effort, but the result is ownership. Choose this if you value infrastructure sovereignty over renting access. For those who prefer renting, wait for Stripe or PayPal to expand—but history shows they won’t.

Stripe, PayPal, and alternatives exclude these regions due to regulatory risk, not your business. Sovereign stacks use globally accessible tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare, and NOWPayments. The Edge Commerce Stack deploys this in 48 hours, configured for your products. Upfront cost is higher, but ownership eliminates recurring fees and platform dependency. If you need permanent sales infrastructure, this is your solution.

Your Deployment Checklist

1. Choose your stack: Edge Commerce Stack for Cloudflare-based infrastructure or Sovereign Starter Stack for GitHub-based deployment. 2. Provide product details: name, description, price, and file links for up to 5 products. 3. Select your payment network: BSC, Solana, or TRON for low transaction fees. 4. Deploy the stack: COREMERCH configures GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments in 48 hours. 5. Test end-to-end: verify payment processing, order storage, and file delivery before going live. 6. Own your system: all code and data are deployed under your accounts—no platform access required.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use the Edge Commerce Stack if I’m not technical?
Yes. The stack is deployed and configured by COREMERCH. You provide product details, and we handle the technical setup. After deployment, the system is designed for non-technical users.
What happens if NOWPayments goes down?
NOWPayments operates as a payment processor, not a platform. If it fails, you can switch to another crypto payment gateway without rebuilding your stack. Your infrastructure remains intact.
Do I need to host my own files?
No. The stack uses Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive for file delivery. You upload files to your own storage, and the system automates delivery upon payment confirmation.
Can I add more products after deployment?
Yes. The stack includes documentation for adding products. You can also purchase additional support for ongoing configuration if needed.
What if I need to refund a customer?
Refunds are handled manually via your crypto wallet. The system does not automate refunds, but you retain full control over your funds and customer relationships.
